title: density filter
explanation:
### Description

Demonstrate vtkPointDensityFilter with four density estimation modes: fixed radius volume-normalized, relative radius number-of-points, weighted fixed radius, and weighted relative radius, displayed as image slices in a 2x2 grid.

**dataset → input → filter → visual_asset → renderer → infrastructure → scene → output**

- [vtkBoundedPointSource](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkBoundedPointSource.html) — bounded point source.
- [vtkClipPolyData](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkClipPolyData.html) — clips polygonal data with an implicit function.
- [vtkFitImplicitFunction](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkFitImplicitFunction.html) — fit implicit function.
- [vtkImageSlice](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkImageSlice.html) — image slice.
- [vtkImageSliceMapper](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkImageSliceMapper.html) — image slice mapper.
- [vtkMath](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkMath.html) — provides mathematical utility functions.
- [vtkPlane](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPlane.html) — defines an implicit plane function.
- [vtkPointDensityFilter](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPointDensityFilter.html) — point density filter.
- [vtkRandomAttributeGenerator](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRandomAttributeGenerator.html) — generates random point and cell data arrays for testing.
- [vtkSphere](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkSphere.html) — defines an implicit sphere function.
- [vtkTimerLog](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkTimerLog.html) — timer log.
- [vtkRenderWindow](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderWindow.html) — displays the rendered scene in a window on screen.
- [vtkRenderWindowInteractor](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderWindowInteractor.html) — captures mouse and keyboard events.
- [vtkRenderer](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderer.html) — assembles the scene and configures the camera.
- `Initialize()` and `Start()` launch the interactive visualization — `Initialize()` prepares the interactor and `Start()` begins the event loop.
